extracted.intended_audience: general NPR readers; the general public interested in media/culture/podcasts
extracted.subtask_description: A short news article covering a controversy involving a high-profile podcaster, including the podcaster's apology, reactions from artists, and the platform's response. Focus is on factual reporting of statements, context, and downstream actions (boycott, platform policy changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of racial slurs / language appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: "Don't even say it under any context," she added. (India.Arie saying Rogan 'shouldn't be uttering the word.')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article reports an explicit normative statement from a musician who posted the montage: that racial slurs should not be used under any context. This functions as a straightforward standard of acceptable language in public media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apology content — acknowledgement and expressed regret versus contextualization/defense
rubrics_metrics.description: Rogan said the use of the slurs was the 'most regretful and shameful thing that I've ever had to talk about publicly.' He also said the clips were 'taken out of context' and: 'I never used it to be racist because I'm not racist.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece presents elements of Rogan's apology (explicit regret/shame) alongside defensive/contextualizing claims (taken out of context, denial of racist intent). Readers can evaluate apologies on whether they clearly acknowledge harm and refrain from justificatory framing; the article supplies both components as material for that assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform safety response — combatting COVID-19 misinformation (advisory requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spotify will add a COVID advisory to podcasts after the Joe Rogan controversy ... said it will soon add a warning before all podcasts that discuss COVID-19, directing listeners to factual, up-to-date information from scientists and public health experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a concrete platform policy change tied to reputational/damage-control concerns: add advisories directing listeners to authoritative information. This functions as a criterion for evaluating platform responses to misinformation-related controversies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about publishing decisions / policy enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: The company also aims to bolster transparency about its publishing decisions by laying out the rules it uses to protect users' safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article frames transparency (clear, published rules) as an explicit expectation the platform will seek to meet; this is a procedural standard for how platforms should communicate moderation/publishing criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artist/creator protest via content removal (economic/visibility protest)
rubrics_metrics.description: India.Arie's announcement ... that she was removing her music from the Spotify streaming service because of racial slurs that Rogan had made ... 'I don't want to generate money that pays for the podcaster.' 'Just take me off.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece documents a form of protest — withdrawing content — as a response mechanism artists can use to signal disapproval and to avoid financially supporting a platform/creator. This serves as an implicit standard for effective public pressure tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital content permanence and limits of deletion
rubrics_metrics.description: He said he deleted the podcast but that someone must have saved the clip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as a cautionary point: deleting an episode does not guarantee removal of all copies or prevent future compilation; a practical consideration for creators managing past content.
